title: Carrier progression can occur without the intended residue bond
statement: The proposed prefix thioester reacts with an aminoacyl incoming-carrier thioester to form the peptoid amide and leave the incoming residue next active end, while the N-terminal origin remains bound. A failed encounter can retry; hydrolysis produces a dead origin-bound acid without free reactivation. A carrier thiol from packet hydrolysis can instead exchange onto the old prefix, changing its outgoing address with no new residue; old thiol can recapture a correct extension and permit duplicate addition. These are explicit chemical bypasses, not merely optical ambiguity.
